final.memo:
Our original thesis for Herbalife was premised on a profitable business being mispriced due to a public controversy and a technical short attack [D01]. This investment was never intended to be a long-term commitment to hold through years of regulatory debate [D01, D06]. 

As of March 1, 2013, the stock has undergone a significant repricing following the initial controversy, and the management rebuttal and latest earnings release are now well-digested by the market [D03, D07]. While the company reported strong sales and volume growth in Q4, this operating performance does not mitigate the underlying legal and business-model criticisms [D01, D03]. 

We have achieved our initial objective. We are not in the business of winning public arguments or waiting indefinitely for regulatory resolution; once the technical squeeze has run its course, our edge is spent [D01]. We choose to take the gain now and rotate capital into more attractive event-driven opportunities [D01, D05].
